Color scale for continuous values (chart)

Source: R/plotly.R
kit_chart_sequential.Rd

Very light lime → light lime (bg-new) → KIT green (nb-green): larger values are darker. For heatmaps and color bars (e.g. pass rates in a response design plot). The minimum is not white, so 0 looks different from an empty cell with no data (white background). kit_plotly_style() switches heatmaps to this scale by default.

Usage

kit_chart_sequential(brand = kit_current_brand())

Arguments

brand

The brand (kit_brand()); defaults to kit_current_brand() (KIT when none is set).

Value

A plotly colorscale: list(list(0, "#F3F7D3"), ..., list(1, "#006835")).

Details

The scale comes from the brand (kit_brand()): 0 is a very light color made by mixing accent_light with white, 0.2 is accent_light, and 0.2 to 1 interpolates in Lab space from accent_light to primary. For the KIT brand these are the values above. Categorical colors (kit_chart_colors(), Okabe–Ito) do not change with the brand: they are colorblind-friendly.

See also

kit_plotly_style(), kit_chart_colors()

kit_chart_sequential()
